scope.brief: art-drop/BRIEF-8.md, Part B: City buildings, 16 + 16 winter. Verdicts apply only to these 32 files.
scope.prior_review: art-drop/review/critic-r8B-0.json does not exist; no prior-pass override applies.
scope.calibration: Good enough to ship beside approved art. Shared construction vocabulary, intentional flat sign faces, small pixel staircases and an empty landing deck are not automatically failures. Each pass survived native, enlarged and scene checks.
scope.references: Part B explicitly retains scifi-city-tower-0..7 and their winter variants as the tallest landmarks, and the shared introduction names approved markers for pixel density. Compared all 16 retained tower sprites, local reference/scifi-marker0..3, approved out/scifi-marker0..3, and out/marker3 examples for fantasy, wuxia, jazz_age, modern and wasteland. Also compared representative approved round-2 city/slums/industry/farmland tiles, paddies in all four seasons, and grass/plains bases in all four seasons with matching composited details.
scope.other_parts: Street bases from Part A are used only as context. Parts C and D receive no verdicts; their slum/industry block QC is outside this requested Part B scope.
scope.inapplicable: No mountain bases/peaks/ridges, crater or ruin props, standalone forest tree sets or autumn files belong to Part B. Peak lattice/range and forest-tree composites have no Part B inputs. Egg-crate peaks, Swiss-cheese craters, classical ruins and flat orange autumn are not applicable. Park trees in building 15 were checked for crown variety in the park and city composites.

checks.coverage_and_scale: Viewed all 32 files at 1x and 4x in size-group/overview/context sheets, and every complete sprite individually at exact nearest-neighbour 8x on both muted olive-grey and its seasonal street. No original asset was resized or changed on disk.
checks.dimensions_and_anchor: All 0-5 are 48x48, all 6-11 are 48x96, all 12-15 are 96x96. All have alpha values only 0 and 255. Nontransparent pixels end on source row 46 for small sprites and row 94 for medium/large (one transparent bottom row). Bounding boxes are centred to within approximately 1 pixel and keep the base on the bottom rows. No canvas-edge cropping.
checks.edges_blur_aa_noise: All 32 have hard pixel edges and compact palettes (15-23 visible RGB colours). At 8x, no interpolation blur, soft antialiasing ramp, matte-colour fringe or stray halo was found on either background. Dark perimeter clusters separate the shapes; selective bright snow-edge breaks are intentional surface highlights rather than a translucent fringe. No independent salt-and-pepper/noise rejection.
checks.lighting_palette_density: Roof and upper-left ledges are light, right/recessed facades dark. No concrete top-left light reversal found. Cool grey/teal facades, pale cream roof rims, warm windows and restrained magenta/cyan fit the approved scifi landmarks. More neon than the older pale marker is expressly requested. Window and roof clusters have compatible pixel density. Hologram 13 has a focal rendering/readability failure rather than a general hue-palette failure.
checks.silhouette_duplicates: Compared each season side by side and summer/winter pairs. Kiosk, arched shop, wedge shop, offset stack, cylinders, terraced offices, stair tower, dish office and all four large functions are distinguishable by geometry and roofline. No exact duplicate or rejection-level near-duplicate within either season. Summer/winter pairing is intentional. The retained tower set still contains the tallest landmark silhouettes.
checks.random_8x2: Both seasons: exact 384x96 strip of 16 one-cell sprites, unrotated/unflipped and selected/shuffled with fixed seed 8101, including all six small variants. Viewed at 1x/4x. No joined tile frames or stamped circuit grid. Individual repeats are recognisable, as expected for a six-prop set, but do not create a continuous cloned texture. Medium and large props are not one-cell tiles and are checked in block scenes instead.
checks.dense_city_block: Both seasons: 576x480 street context, all 16 Part B designs and all eight retained seasonal towers, plus 40 repeated small/medium buildings; 64 placed props total. Large props reserve 2x2 ground cells; other props anchor in individual cells and may overlap vertically like planted trees. Bottom-depth sorting and a clear 96-pixel road corridor. Viewed native and four exact 4x quadrants covering the whole scene, as well as full saved 4x. Shop fronts, warm/cool glazing, terraces and landmarks read as a neon settlement rather than a stamped cyberpunk texture. The glyph on 13 remains visibly pasted/flat. Winter ground pattern is contextual Part A material, not a reason to fail these building files.
checks.bases_3x3: Part B contains no bases. For the requested ground-context check, made literal 3x3 unrotated seasonal street-base repeats, saved/viewed at 1x/4x with exact 4x four-tile-join windows. No hard tile-boundary gap is introduced by the building sprites. Any ground texture repetition belongs to Part A and receives no Part B verdict.
checks.winter: All 16 winter sprites preserve their corresponding design, have visible snow on horizontal receiving surfaces and retain neon/windows. Dark blue-grey snow shadows fit the approved winter art. The cleared landing deck is consistent with an operational pad; white rim, cabin and ramp ledges make winter unambiguous. Park crowns are varied and snow-covered. No blank winter, indiscriminate white wash or independent seasonal-consistency failure.

scifi-city-bldg-0.assessment: Low asymmetric shop, magenta awning, warm storefront and projecting roof equipment remain legible at native size. Distinct from the other five small buildings.

scifi-city-bldg-1.assessment: Round kiosk and narrow aerial give a clear small silhouette. Glass, roof rim and door separate at native size; the outline is clean.

scifi-city-bldg-2.assessment: Two-storey shop with a stepped upper roof, side stair and vertical sign. Warm and cool windows are separated rather than speckled randomly.

scifi-city-bldg-3.assessment: Arched ribbed roof and central entrance distinguish this low block. Roof ribs converge consistently and remain readable in the random strip.

scifi-city-bldg-4.assessment: Narrow wedge roof and front canopy make a distinctly different silhouette. The cyan roof panel stays within the roof plane; no detached fringe or reversed light.

scifi-city-bldg-5.assessment: Three offset glazed tiers remain distinct from the two-storey shop and stepped medium blocks. Strong cool window masses are balanced by warm windows and dark framing.

scifi-city-bldg-6.assessment: Tall narrow terraced block with roof vents and vertical magenta billboard. Warm window rhythm is readable, not random noise; setbacks are clear.

scifi-city-bldg-7.assessment: Rounded glazed mid-rise with a broad roof deck, antenna and raised rooftop enclosure. Alternating warm and cool window bands read cleanly in context.

scifi-city-bldg-8.assessment: Split roofline, rooftop sign/dome and exterior zigzag stair give an unmistakably different profile. Stair is small but coherent at native size.

scifi-city-bldg-9.assessment: Shorter mid-rise with paired roof vents and a large side billboard. Its lower height and offset mass distinguish it from 6 and 10; the blank sign face is an acceptable small sign.

scifi-city-bldg-10.assessment: Broad tapering terraced mid-rise with planted ledges and roof machinery. Similar construction language to 6, but different width, setbacks, roofline and signage; not a near-duplicate.

scifi-city-bldg-11.assessment: Round-cornered office block with dish and aerial, cyan glazing and magenta belt. Dish is crisp and the building differs clearly from the roof-deck cylinder 7.

scifi-city-bldg-12.assessment: Wide U-shaped megablock with recessed court, multiple wings and shops. Court, wings and storefronts remain separable at native scale; acceptable detail density beside the retained towers.

scifi-city-bldg-13.problems: The central hologram (approximately source x30-64/y33-68) reads as a solid, flat cyan outlined glyph/scaffold pasted onto a shaded plaza. Its broad strokes use essentially one mid-value cyan, with no bright emission core, projected breaks or light interaction with the plinth. At 1x it resembles a musical-note icon; at 4x/8x its uniform fill and heavy dark border stand apart from the articulated lit windows, signs and retained landmark art. The plaza underneath is adequately drawn, but the focal object does not convincingly read as a luminous holographic sculpture. Redraw the glyph with a few controlled bright cyan/pale cores and darker cyan edge clusters, clarify which strokes cross or sit behind others, and introduce one or two deliberate projection gaps or a small crisp light reflection on the plinth. Keep the effect pixel-sharp and restrained: no blurred glow, antialiasing or added speckle. Retest the isolated sprite and dense city at native size.

scifi-city-bldg-14.assessment: Landing platform reads immediately from its large clear deck, cyan broken ring, control cabin and access ramp. The calm central fill is functional landing space, not muddy or unfinished texture.

scifi-city-bldg-15.assessment: Small landscaped park reads as paths, raised planters, fountain and trees. Crowns differ in width, height and lobe arrangement; they are not identical stamps. Broad foliage clusters fit the limited sprite scale.

scifi-city@winter-bldg-0.assessment: Low asymmetric shop, magenta awning, warm storefront and projecting roof equipment remain legible at native size. Distinct from the other five small buildings. Snow follows the corresponding roofs/ledges or landscape surfaces, retains blue-grey shadow clusters and leaves the defining architecture and neon readable. This is a visible seasonal treatment, not a blank export or global tint.
